item.title: From Columbus, Georgia to the World: The Enduring Legacy of Alma Thomas
item.description: Today, the story of Alma Thomas is being told in its entirety. She was a brilliant, disciplined, visionary artist who spent decades refining her voice before the world was ready to listen. As her full story comes into focus, it is time for the world to recognize what Columbus, Georgia has always known: Alma Thomas’s story is a vibrant part of Columbus, Georgia

item.title: Columbus, Georgia Lights Up Local Stories: Film Office Doubles Down on Homegrown Filmmaking for 2026
item.description: In a city where artistry meets riverfront grit, Columbus, Georgia continues to rise as a place where stories are not just told—but made. This year, the Columbus Film Office has announced a bold expansion to its Local Filmmaker Grant Program, deepening its investment in the voices and visions emerging from the Chattahoochee Valley.

item.title: A Work of Heart: Why You Should Consider Giving Local Art This Valentine’s Day
item.description: Written by TJ ShockleyValentine’s Day has a way of sneaking up on us. item.title: An “Immortal Play About Mortal People" –
item.description: “Our Town,” an iconic, heart-wrenching Pulitzer Prize-winning play by Thornton Wilder, is coming to our town, Columbus, Georgia. This classic show will open on February 13th and come to life on Family Theatre’s stage, located at 2100 Hamilton Road, nestled beneath Rosehill Baptist Church.

item.title: Inside Riverdance’s 30th Anniversary Tour: A Conversation with Principal Dancer Kieran Bryant
item.description: When Riverdance arrives in Columbus this February, audiences will experience a landmark moment in the show’s history: its 30th Anniversary Tour, featuring a new generation of dancers carrying forward one of the world’s most beloved productions.

item.description: Written by Yinuo ChenThe CSU Guitar Symposium has become one of the most exciting events of the year for guitarists and audiences.
